title: Galois transitivity on fibres of an affine base change
statement: Let k and K be fields with a possibly infinite Galois extension K/k. Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a morphism f:X -> Spec(k) [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let p:X_K -> X be the first projection of its base change [def-pc-base-change]. For points x,y of X_K with p(x)=p(y), there is a k-algebra automorphism sigma of K for which (id_X times Spec(sigma))(x)=y. This is the action on scheme points, not merely rational points.

proof.text: Write the affine scheme as `Spec A`, using its canonical `isoSpec`, and give `A` its `k`-algebra structure through the ring map corresponding to `f`. The pullback is `Spec (A ⊗[k] K)`, by `pullbackSpecIso`. The two points correspond to prime ideals with the same contraction to `A`; the action is `Spec (id_A ⊗ σ)`.

Equip `G = Aut(K/k)` with its Krull topology, which is profinite for any Galois algebraic extension, including an infinite one. Equip `A ⊗[k] K` with the discrete topology and let `G` act on the right tensor factor. Each tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. The subgroup fixing its finitely many right-hand coefficients is open, so the action is continuous. The action commutes with the `A`-scalars. Exact Mathlib tools: CompactSpace Gal(K/k) in FieldTheory/Galois/Profinite.lean, stabilizer_isOpen_of_isIntegral in KrullTopology.lean, and continuousSMul_iff_stabilizer_isOpen in Topology/Algebra/MulAction.lean. A subgroup containing an open subgroup is open.

The fixed field of `G` is `k`. Apply `TensorProduct.injective_and_range_eq_invariants` with the full automorphism group to the underlying vector space of `A`. Thus the invariant ring of the tensor product is precisely the image of `A`, giving `Algebra.IsInvariant A (A ⊗[k] K) G`. The infinite fixed-field input is InfiniteGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed in FieldTheory/Galois/Infinite.lean, rather than the finite-dimensional theorem of Galois/Basic.lean.

Apply `Algebra.IsInvariant.exists_smul_of_under_eq_of_profinite` to the two primes. Its ideal action is direct image under the ring automorphism, whereas `Spec` uses inverse image. Replace the supplied automorphism by its inverse. Transport the resulting equality through the affine comparison. This gives exactly the displayed equality of points.

lean.statement: theorem exists_galois_map_eq_of_affine_projection_eq (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsGalois k K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x y : ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) (hxy : (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) x = (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) y) : ∃ σ : K ≃ₐ[k] K, (baseChangeMap f (specAlgEquivOver σ)) x = y
